query: For additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 high-entropy alloy with an fcc matrix, what testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs degradation during elevated-temperature exposure to oxidizing or reducing gases and why catastrophic failure may occur? Specify a controlled change that would reveal the governing behavior, predicted observations relative to the starting-state baseline, applicable exposure boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a clear falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Selective internal oxidation of Ti at fcc grain boundaries governs embrittlement and catastrophic failure of the AM Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 HEA during high‐temperature exposure in oxidizing atmospheres.  Enriching the Ti content by 50% will promote formation of a continuous, protective Ti‐rich oxide scale on the surface, reducing internal oxygen penetration along grain boundaries and thereby preserving ductility and strength.
generation.material_initial_state: As‐printed additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 HEA with single‐phase fcc matrix, average grain size ~10 μm, baseline Ti content 0.3 at.%
generation.intervention: Increase Ti content from 0.3 at.% to 0.45 at.% during alloy composition step; all other processing parameters held constant
generation.conditions: Exposure in dry O2 atmosphere, T=800 °C, pO2=0.21 bar, t=100 h (also test T=600–900 °C and pO2=0.01–1 bar, t up to 1000 h)
generation.structural_mediator: Continuity and thickness of Ti‐rich surface oxide scale and depth of internal oxide penetration along grain boundaries
generation.mechanism: Higher Ti availability drives preferential formation of a dense TiOx layer at the surface, which slows inward oxygen diffusion and suppresses internal Ti oxide nucleation at grain boundaries; this preserves matrix cohesion and ductility
generation.predicted_outcome: Ti-enriched alloy will show ~25% thinner internal oxide penetration depth at grain boundaries, ~20% lower scale spallation, and ~15% higher retained fracture toughness after 100 h at 800 °C compared to the baseline alloy
generation.baseline: Original AM Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy after 100 h at 800 °C in O2, measured internal oxide depth, scale spallation, and fracture toughness
generation.boundary: Valid for T=600–900 °C, pO2=0.01–1 bar, exposure time up to 1000 h
generation.uncertainty: Moderate, as direct data on Ti scale continuity in this specific HEA system are limited

falsification_experiment.design: Produce two AM HEA variants (Ti=0.3 at.% and Ti=0.45 at.%). Expose both to 800 °C in pO2=0.21 bar for 100 h. Characterize oxide scale and internal penetration by cross‐sectional SEM/TEM; measure fracture toughness (K_IC) post‐exposure.
measurements: internal oxide penetration depth along grain boundaries
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Ti-enriched variant shows equal or greater internal oxide penetration depth, no reduction in scale spallation, or no improvement (±5%) in fracture toughness relative to the baseline Ti=0.3 at.% alloy, the hypothesis is falsified.
